transcript.dialogue: A ghost podcast and gulls? That is way wilder than anything I usually do, I'm kind of into it.
Well, the gulls are tough critics, but maybe you've got a decent ghost story in you before that arcade machine explodes.
Oh, I've got a couple wild stories, but let's go play that broken game first and see if we can actually win something for once.
Lead the way, but if it tries to interrupt my ghost story, I'm unplugging it.
Deal, but first we gotta dodge my ex walking over right now—wanna hide behind this pinball machine?
An ex? Perfect, maybe they can tell us a decent haunting tale while we crouch here.
You are hilarious, let's definitely grab drinks and swap stories after this craziness ends.
Drinks and ghost stories it is, but you're buying the round if my boots get sticky on the arcade floor.

recap.setting: A loud retro arcade where one broken machine keeps announcing a winner amidst flashing neon lights.
scenes: Jordan approaches Juniper near the flashing pinball machines, striking a cool pose while Juniper quietly studies a gull graphic on the wall.
Suddenly, an old rival from Jordan's past arrives demanding a rematch on the broken machine, creating complete chaos.
Juniper decides it is time to depart for the evening, leaving Jordan wanting another round while Juniper considers a future meetup.
recap.best_line: Even the gulls have better timing than this.

judge.note: The biggest problem is Jordan instantly knowing about Juniper's podcast despite being on a blind date, though the deadpan banter about the ex behind the pinball machine has some charm.

transcript.dialogue: Well, a cold beach at midnight is dramatic enough to earn a pastry, provided you promise not to call my croissants 'just carbs.'
Call them carbs if they lack a soul, or if they're store-bought. Have you ever baked while a phantom rapped on the lighthouse glass?
Only if the phantom has decent taste and brings a proper appetite for brown butter brioche!
Brioche won't save you if the phantom wants answers, Rafe. Do you believe in spirits, or are you just here for the snacks?
I am strictly here for the snacks, but I'll fight any ghost who insults my brioche!
A fighter of pastries, how brave. Let's see if your courage holds when the floorboards groan at three in the morning.
Honestly, fighting invisible seagulls in the dark sounds exhausting, so I think I'm heading back to my oven.
If you flee from creaking wood, you'd never survive a real haunting anyway. Safe travels to your oven.

recap.setting: A cold beach at night featuring one shared blanket and a thermos of terrible tea.
scenes: Rafe greets Juniper with a flour-dusted grin expecting applause, while Juniper stares unbothered from beneath a massive storm coat.
A long, awkward silence settles over the beach as the terrible thermos tea makes both of them regret their life choices.
They mutually agree the date is an absolute disaster and decide to leave together to find better snacks.
recap.best_line: This tea tastes like liquid fog and despair.

judge.note: The voices are vivid and distinct, though the mutual rejection at the end feels slightly rushed rather than fully earned.

transcript.dialogue: Nineteen times? Well, that definitely beats my personal record for most accidental detours into wet cement!
Wet cement has a certain gravity to it, though at least it doesn't try to catch a breeze.
That is remarkably fair! Though I suppose you're used to things being up in flames, quite literally.
I prefer my warmth safely contained inside a kiln these days, away from any sudden drafts.
Kilns are great, though I once tried to map one and ended up drawing a toaster instead!
Toasters have a way of throwing people off, but honesty usually leaves a much better blueprint. Do you ever draw outside the lines on purpose?
Only if the lines lead somewhere entirely unexpected, preferably with better tea!
I can certainly get behind better tea, as long as there are no hidden surprises waiting at the bottom of the cup.

recap.setting: A cramped corner café that is closing in an hour, chairs going up around them under the hum of dim neon lights.
scenes: Mira arrives with ink-stained cuffs, immediately sketching a rough map of the café on a napkin, while Dex offers a very careful handshake with clay still dried to his elbows.
As the chairs scrape upward around them, Dex suddenly admits that he flinches at birthday candles and spent his past career getting set on fire professionally.
They share a warm laugh over the absurdity of their lives, realizing they are kindred spirits who prefer a low-stakes evening.
recap.best_line: I fold maps the way I live my life: completely upside down and hoping for the best.

judge.note: The biggest problem is Mira knowing about the nineteen fires without Dex saying it; the best moment is Dex's grounded pottery imagery balancing her frantic energy.

transcript.dialogue: You've got dirt under your nails and half a forest in that tote—careful, if you start planting me, I might actually stay still.
I promise I only plant things where the soil is stubborn and the city forgets to look.
Well, the soil here is certainly stubborn, but I assure you, everyone is looking right now.
Let's talk about anything else before the sky opens up and ruins your polished shoes.
Fair enough, let's keep it light—make me laugh before the rain does and I'll forgive the threat to my footwear.
If I wanted to make you laugh, I'd tell you about the time I tried to waltz with a parking meter, but let's just enjoy the breeze instead.
A parking meter? Oh, please tell me you at least let it lead.
Obviously not, I have much better posture than a parking meter.

recap.setting: A botanic park in the minutes before it rains, where neither Teo nor Inés is willing to mention the heavy grey sky.
scenes: Teo stands with perfect posture and an unbuttoned collar, while Inés arrives with dirt under her nails and a tote of seedlings.
As the first drops of rain begin to fall, Inés suddenly admits she has illegally planted thirty-one trees in city roundabouts without permission.
After sharing a hearty laugh over the roundabout rebellion, Teo abruptly stands up and announces he must leave immediately to beat the storm.
recap.best_line: If the city council catches me, tell them my trees died innocent.

judge.note: The best moment is Inés joking about the parking meter, which immediately brings out Teo's competitive ballroom vanity; the biggest problem is the repetitive physical stage directions for Teo adjusting his collar.

transcript.dialogue: Forty-one party hats and zero dining tables is an architectural choice I can only assume lacks structural integrity.
Who needs a table when you can eat cake off a disco ball? Drop the pencil and grab a tambourine!
Eating off a glass sphere sounds like a maintenance nightmare, but I suppose precision takes a backseat to chaos here.
Precision is boring, Orin! Jump in the ball pit before Wally notices we're off-script!
A ball pit is technically a hazard, but seeing as you haven't caused a structural collapse yet, lead the way.
That is the absolute best 'yes' I have ever heard! Cannonball!
I reserve the right to complain about the upholstery later, but I'm coming in.
You actually jumped! Okay, you're officially my favorite hazard inspector ever!

recap.setting: A vibrant karaoke booth booked for a full hour, with a pre-queued song blinking on the screen and a protective chaperone hovering by the door.
scenes: Orin adjusts his reading glasses on their chain, noting the karaoke screen's song title contains a grammatical error, while Sable bursts into the booth wearing three different patterns and a party hat.
The booth's automated booking system suddenly crashes and deletes the entire song queue, forcing them to improvise entertainment using only a tambourine and a dry-erase marker.
Orin meticulously counts the remaining minutes on his watch, politely shakes Sable's glitter-covered hand, and departs first, leaving both wishing for another round despite the parting.
recap.best_line: Technically, that lyric lacks both subject and verb.

judge.note: Orin knows Sable's exact hat and table count without her mentioning it, but the friction between his exactitude and her chaos is delightful.

transcript.dialogue: Eleven tiny courses? Let's skip the small talk and eat every single one of them at once.
Eleven courses means eleven timed courses, though, right? Or are you a simultaneous-plate anarchist?
Total anarchist. I'll take all eleven plates piled high right now, no waiting!
I respect the ambition, but the culinary logistics alone would trigger a minor security incident.
Security incidents are just high-speed floor plans. Let's breach the kitchen and assemble them ourselves!
Breaching the kitchen violates at least four health codes, but I love a well-organized heist. Lead the way.

recap.setting: A too-fancy tasting-menu restaurant with eleven tiny courses and a hovering waiter, bathed in harsh speed-dating strobe lights.
scenes: Kaz slides into the booth with chalk-dusted palms and blurts out a crane-climbing story, while Nell instantly rattles off the exact architectural history of the restaurant ceiling under a glaring ten-minute countdown.
When the hovering waiter drops the entire eleven-course tray onto the floor, the strict schedule collapses instantly and they have to improvise dinner using breadsticks and stolen salt shakers.
With the clock flashing red, Kaz asks a sharp follow-up about Nell's favorite marble bust, and Nell matches Kaz's restless energy by proposing they sneak out the kitchen fire escape together.
recap.best_line: Who needs eleven tiny courses when we can scale the fire escape right now?

judge.note: The best moment is Nell matching Kaz's restless energy with logistics; the biggest problem is that it reads more like a sketch than a real date.
